primary_evidence_gate.execution: data-only; do not execute or import the guest helper
required_inputs: Exact case JSON and SHA-256 for each pinned helper and suite; frozen candidate hash and VM provenance.

Runner setup/candidate result and all case-listed diagnostic records including base64 bytes, missing/error flags, captured byte counts and truncation flags; targeted cases additionally list network-native-target.json.
Each decoded network control and candidate record including raw trace bytes, parsed events, stdout/stderr, status/termination, snapshots and assessment.
retention_rules: For a completed stage require all case-listed diagnostic files, each regular, readable, present, nontruncated and valid JSON; reject inconsistent byte counts or hashes. Reject duplicate JSON keys and unexpected control-label multiplicities; repeated baseline/post-candidate ip labels are reconciled as ordered per-snapshot occurrences, while native-target labels are unique within their labeled interval.

For a failed setup, require only records from stages actually reached; retain available compiler, parser, outer, stage, control and candidate records without inventing absent later records. Missing stage-appropriate records mean ERROR/incomplete, not candidate mismatch.

A trace or stream prefix intentionally captured after a timeout or output/trace limit is explicitly partial in its record; it is not an externally truncated diagnostic file. It can support a failure only when actual begin-marker evidence exists; it can never support a PASS.

For a native-target setup failure, require network-native-target.json once its capture stage has started; inspect state, before/control/after progress, snapshots and errors conditionally. Before is retained before any native-target attempt. After is attempted and incrementally retained even if the target observer/control fails; a before-capture failure has no target invocation and no after requirement. Missing reached-stage diagnostics are ERROR/incomplete.

identity_rules.uuid_rule: Require canonical identical marker and protected /run attestation bytes for both outer and inner identity records. Bind both UUIDs to primary VM provenance and its independently root-validated attestation readback, including matching marker/attestation bytes and the case-insensitively matching root DMI UUID. Do not require an unprivileged DMI product_uuid read or invent a product_uuid observation in the fixture.
identity_rules.protected_files: For each outer and inner marker and attestation record, require the literal directory_path and entry_name (/etc/bashos-parity-vm or /run/bashos-parity-vm-identity), entry_follow_symlinks=false, and recorded Linux directory_open_flags with O_DIRECTORY, O_NOFOLLOW and O_CLOEXEC and file_open_flags with O_NONBLOCK, O_NOFOLLOW and O_CLOEXEC, both read-only. Independently decode each raw_mode to verify its type and permission mode fields. Require directory_before, directory and directory_entry to be directories and match type, raw_mode, uid, gid, dev and ino; require non-group/world-writable permissions. Require file_before, file and file_entry all regular and identical across type, raw_mode, uid, gid, mode, nlink, size, dev, ino, mtime_ns and ctime_ns; require mode 0444, one link, 37 bytes, and exact canonical UUID plus newline. Independently validate controller root attestation write/read proof status, raw evidence and matching readback with unique JSON keys and root DMI/marker/attestation bytes. Bind each fixture file to its corresponding controller readback marker or attestation on type, mode, nlink, size, dev, ino, mtime_ns and ctime_ns and bytes. Bind each fixture parent to corresponding etc_directory or run_directory on type, mode, dev and ino. Require controller ownership root:root, outer root:root and inner ownership equal to kernel overflow uid/gid under the exact one-id uid/gid maps; compare other invariant fields across outer and inner as well. Directory size, nlink and timestamps may legitimately change and are retained but not equality prerequisites. Reject missing fields, duplicate keys, inconsistent types, symlink entries, mismatched objects, invalid ownership or incomplete proofs as infrastructure ERROR/incomplete, never as product mismatch. Require completed systemd virtualization check and QEMU vendor; do not read root-only product_uuid in fixture.
identity_rules.candidate_cap_rule: post-exec CapEff must include CAP_NET_ADMIN for keep and exclude it for drop
identity_rules.outer_setup: finished with status 0 for a complete observation; failed/unavailable namespace, dummy, gcc, ptrace, parser or native control is ERROR

native_control_rules: Require each scenario's listed labels exactly once and in the listed order, all marked mode; status, stdout/stderr, capability mode and full raw trace must agree with the declared control.

Reparse raw traces independently and compare parsed events with stored events. Each native trace must contain exactly begin then end markers and exactly one matching successful guard SIOCGIFFLAGS for the declared guard before begin and one after end. The inside events must exactly match the listed ordered requests; unrelated outside-window ioctl events do not count as inside.

Validate native address and route ip/proc readbacks, and for native-auto verify both eligible interfaces plus unbound default route via bn0 in both ip JSON and proc route. Validate scenario-specific native-target fields/status and unchanged before state when listed.

Require native-mark-empty with zero inside ioctls, while both outside guard requests are observed. This and each marked positive/error native control exercise the same observer marker path used for the candidate.
trace_integrity: Reject malformed records, duplicate exec or exit, invalid marker order, mismatched window labels, observer_error, unobserved child/fork/clone or trace parse inconsistency. Require post-exec capability and tracer status zero for completed captures.

For a normal operation require exactly exec, begin and end markers, one final exit, complete non-prefix trace, and all inside-window ioctl events in order. Require candidate argv, scenario, mode, termination, output lengths and trace to agree across controls, observation, stage and assessment.

For a normal candidate early exit or signal with a complete valid trace but no begin or no end, classify FAIL early-exit or operation-interrupted; retain raw output/status and do not infer any successful operation, ioctl absence, or kernel result.

For timeout/output-limit/trace-limit require a valid partial trace with exec and actual begin marker. Begin without end is operation-limit FAIL; begin and end is post-operation-limit FAIL, not an operation timeout. Validate observed-length/prefix metadata and retain partial bytes; do not assert later operation results.

Interruption before begin is unresolved startup/infrastructure ERROR, even if exec was seen; preserve partial trace and output. If no exec, marker, parse, controls or observer integrity can be established, classify ERROR/incomplete.

For complete operation-exited observations, independently recompute each scenario's status, output, errno, request order/fields and kernel expectations below, then cross-check assessment failures and runner outcome. Treat an assessment crash, missing/malformed assessment or inconsistency as ERROR, not product FAIL.

If post-candidate snapshot or later infrastructure fails, retain ERROR for that stage; separately preserve any independently established exit/status/output or complete marked-trace mismatch as product FAIL. Do not infer a pass or a kernel observation from missing data.

Reject a tracee fork, vfork or clone observed at any window, including startup or teardown: the single-tracee observer cannot inspect descendants. A trace or stream limit before a proven begin marker is unresolved even if the shell was execed.

kernel_checks.unchanged: Full recorded pre/post interface, flags, ip route and proc route state equal.
kernel_checks.unchanged-bad-mask: Same unchanged requirement and no inside ioctl; separately retain actual before_bn0 and after_bn0 including any partial mutation, without changing the literal contract.
kernel_checks.addr: bn0 IPv4 192.0.2.20/24 and ioctl-readback flags include IFF_UP and IFF_RUNNING.
kernel_checks.default-bn0: One default via 192.0.2.1 dev bn0 in ip and /proc/net/route, proc mask 0 and flags include RTF_UP|RTF_GATEWAY.
kernel_checks.default-bn1: One default via 192.0.2.1 dev bn1 in ip and proc, mask 0 and flags include 3; native unbound control selected bn0.
kernel_checks.default-bn0-repeat: Before already contains the same default via bn0, native-target returns EEXIST without changing it, and after still contains it with proc mask 0 and flags include 3.

comparison_conventions.inside_ioctl_list: Exact length and order; each listed field must match. flags_all is a bitmask inclusion test; omitted fields are not compared.
comparison_conventions.stderr_contains: Nonempty substring in raw stderr; when empty stderr must be exactly empty. stdout must be exactly empty.

fixture_preconditions.addr_cases: Before candidate bn0 and bn1 are present without IPv4 addresses and there is no default route in either ip or proc.
fixture_preconditions.route_cases: Before candidate bn0 has 192.0.2.20/24, bn1 has 192.0.2.30/24, and both are up. A marked native unbound route must select bn0 and then be removed. The pre-candidate main table has no default in ip or proc except route-repeat.
fixture_preconditions.route-repeat: A native ip command seeds a default via 192.0.2.1 dev bn0. Both ip and proc show it, flags include 3, then marked native-target returns EEXIST and leaves the complete fixture snapshot unchanged.
fixture_preconditions.ipv4_snapshot_evidence: For each bn0/bn1 snapshot, independently validate the exact ordered successful ip -j -4 addr show dev NAME command and its complete raw stdout/stderr. A single IPv4 record must have the matching name, positive integer ifindex a string flags list and an addr_info list containing only inet records; snapshot address_query=record, link_json=null and json must exactly match that raw record. An empty array is not proof that the interface exists: require the immediately following successful ip -j link show dev NAME, exactly one matching-name link with positive integer ifindex and string flags, snapshot address_query=empty, exact link_json, and derived json exactly {ifname, ifindex, addr_info: []} from those data. Never accept empty IPv4 output alone as proof of a device. Validate successful independent SIOCGIFFLAGS for the same interface from the full 40-byte ifreq: name and decoded flags must match the snapshot, and IFF_UP must agree with the UP flag in the relevant ip address or link record; require both bn0 and bn1. For labeled native-target before and after captures require the matching uniquely labeled IPv4 and conditional link controls within each snapshot interval. For other captures reconcile the ordered controls with the corresponding baseline and post-candidate snapshots. Reject missing, failed, duplicate, inconsistent, truncated, malformed or ambiguous controls as infrastructure ERROR/incomplete. This derivation applies only to an actual empty IPv4 array; no address may be silently discarded.

decision_examples.capture: all controls complete; candidate exec and complete exit, no begin marker
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Candidate shell exited early; no ioctl or operation result is inferred.

decision_examples.capture: all controls complete; begin marker present; candidate exits before end marker
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Retain raw trace and exit; do not infer completed operation.

decision_examples.capture: all controls complete; timeout or limit with exec but no begin marker
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Retain partial output and trace; do not attribute operation behavior.

decision_examples.capture: all controls complete; timeout or limit with begin and no end marker
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Retain bounded output and trace prefix; no completed operation claim.

decision_examples.capture: all controls complete; timeout or limit with both markers
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Do not label it operation timeout; retain bounded output and trace prefix.

decision_examples.capture: required controls or stage records missing, malformed, mismatched or externally truncated
decision_examples.evidence_scope: No migration evidence from generic runner labels.

decision_examples.capture: valid complete product trace and wrong status; later state snapshot or assessment is missing
decision_examples.classification: ERROR: incomplete state or assessment; separately preserve established product status mismatch
decision_examples.evidence_scope: No state or PASS claim; product mismatch is not erased.

decision_examples.capture: complete controls, trace and state but saved assessment disagrees with independent recomputation
decision_examples.evidence_scope: Do not promote generic runner result.

binding.control_label: Must equal native-target and bind to exactly one corresponding network-controls trace record.
binding.ordering: Before snapshot completion event precedes native-target control event, which precedes after snapshot completion event. Check matching scenario and digest in each completion event. Check each labeled ip observation for bn0, bn1 and routes occurs in its corresponding snapshot interval. For an empty IPv4 result, the corresponding labeled link response must immediately follow that interface IPv4 response within the same capture interval.
binding.digest: For each complete snapshot, SHA-256 over ASCII JSON with sorted keys, ensure_ascii=true and separators comma/colon without spaces must equal both the item sha256 and its ordered controls event snapshot_sha256.

complete_snapshot_checks: Each labeled item has state complete and step complete; its snapshot contains exactly bn0 and bn1 interfaces, each with the validated IPv4-derived json, address_query, link_json, integer ioctl flags and flags_raw_b64, plus a parsed routes list, raw proc_route text and parsed kernel_defaults.

Independently decode each flags_raw_b64 as the full 40-byte x86_64 ifreq, require its NUL-terminated name to match the interface, and decode the unsigned native-little-endian flags at offset 16; it must equal the recorded flags integer.

Independently parse each saved proc_route and require it to agree with kernel_defaults; apply fixture_preconditions.ipv4_snapshot_evidence to each uniquely labeled raw interface response and conditional link proof, and require raw route stdout to agree with the snapshot routes.

Compare complete before and after snapshots as full values, including both raw and decoded flags, IPv4-derived interface JSON, query markers, conditional full link JSON, routes, raw proc_route and parsed defaults. Independently require exact equality; do not trust the equal field.

Require fixture_baseline to equal the before snapshot. If candidate was reached, independently require network-observation.before to equal that same snapshot. Also verify scenario-specific baseline and native-target ioctl status and request fields against the per-case data.
failure_rules: A missing, truncated, malformed, mislabeled, mismatched, incomplete, incorrectly ordered or unequal required snapshot or failed native-target control is setup ERROR/incomplete and cannot establish candidate product failure or coverage.

For setup errors after capture begins, retain the latest partial item with its step, partial snapshot and error; preserve fixture_baseline and any raw controls event records already produced. If the target was attempted, require an after attempt and preserve its complete or partial result even when native-target itself failed.

If before capture fails or differs from fixture_baseline, no target invocation is attempted and the after snapshot remains not-started. Do not demand records for unattempted later stages or infer native-target behavior.

On a control mismatch or observer error, the artifact remains setup-error after the after attempt, and candidate is not executed. Compare any complete before and after for diagnosis, but never reinterpret the control failure as a candidate failure.
